answer: Each epoch, a randomness beacon streams a challenge word into the inlet of every agent, who must weave it into a signed response to a live task, like summarizing a fresh document with that word. Sybils cannot precompute template answers because the word is unknown until the epoch opens, so each fake identity needs real inference per round. Cost scales linearly with identities, a mirror of honest work, while honest agents pay once. A fleet of thousands burns GPU budget each epoch for capped rewards, so the ledge between expense and payoff collapses.
